description: Kindle/KU fiction reviewer-cluster panel. Each member is a genre/subgenre reader segment; `weight` is that segment's approximate share of the modeled Amazon Kindle + Kindle Unlimited fiction *reading* market (weights sum to 100, so a poll's p_hat reads directly as % of the market). Weights are calibrated to PUBLIC genre-market signals (K-lytics-style analysis), NOT scraped from proprietary K-lytics reports or live BSR/KU dashboards. Replace weights with your K-lytics subscription figures and refine segments/prose from your own reviewer datasets + value-shift tags. See FORK_NOTES.md.
sources: Romance ~40%+ of Kindle sales, ~81% avg KU penetration; romance+fantasy >60% of KU top earners (Robertson Kindle-market genre breakdown; K-lytics Romance report page; Write-A-Catalyst KU genres).
Romantasy/fantasy-romance now outsells traditional fantasy ~3:1 and leads reader demand (K-lytics Fantasy-Romance report; Arkham House 2026 genre trends).
Fantasy ~13%, Sci-Fi ~8%, Thriller ~7%, Mystery/Thriller ~1/5 of Kindle sales (Robertson).

Genre reader skews: romance heavily female; sci-fi male-skewed; fantasy gender-balanced & younger; LitRPG/progression younger-male gamer, Royal Road->KU; cozy mystery older-female; literary fiction older, purchase/print-skewed (YouGov; Sisters in Crime consumer report; Marketing Charts; New Book Recommendation).

members.name: Ashley
members.persona: Reads 15+ KU romances a month; reviews center on whether the emotional promise was kept. A gut-punch that threatens the central relationship reads as a broken contract.

members.name: Maya
members.persona: Drove the romantasy boom; tolerates darkness and betrayal AS LONG AS the romance thread is protected. Posts emotional reviews to a large BookTok following that can make or break a launch.

members.name: Sirena
members.persona: Seeks out exactly the betrayals cozier readers flee; rates a story higher when it has the nerve to hurt her. A well-built double-cross is a selling point in her reviews.

members.name: Danielle
members.persona: Long-haul series reader; forgives darkness if the bond stays sacred, but a mentor-figure betrayal that taints the mate bond will show up as a one-star warning.

members.name: Gwen
members.persona: Wants the betrayal AND the reassurance; enjoys being fooled if the clues were fair and the couple survives the fallout.

members.name: Doran
members.persona: Judges a story by whether it follows through on its own stakes; a fairly-foreshadowed mentor betrayal is exactly the kind of nerve he praises.

members.name: Trevor
members.segment: progression-fantasy / LitRPG reader (KU-native, Royal Road pipeline)
members.persona: Binges 200k-word serials; tolerant of rough prose, merciless about betrayed build-up. A twist that stalls the protagonist's growth annoys him more than it moves him.

members.name: Renee
members.persona: Wants a heroine who sees the betrayal coming and acts; respects a twist that tests the lead rather than one that just victimizes her.

members.name: Kwame
members.persona: Forgives a dark turn the premise has been arguing for; rejects a twist that only works if characters act stupidly.

members.name: Bethany
members.persona: Lives for the betrayal reveal; her top reviews are the ones where she 'never saw it coming but should have.' A clued mentor double-cross is the product she's buying.

members.name: Elspeth
members.persona: Reads to feel safe; a permanent, somber mentor betrayal breaks the cozy promise and she'll flag it as too dark for the shelf she recommends from.

members.name: Frank
members.persona: Grades a betrayal on whether the clues were on the page; a fairly-foreshadowed mentor reveal earns his respect, an out-of-nowhere one earns a lecture.

members.name: Wren
values: no betrayal of the safe cast
members.persona: Came for tea-shop comfort; a permanent mentor betrayal is precisely the tonal violation the subgenre exists to avoid, and her review will say so.

members.name: Helene
members.persona: Writes long structural reviews and drives book-club picks; forgives any dark turn the theme has been quietly arguing for since page one.

members.name: Sam
members.persona: Hand-sells to teens and orders for the collection; weighs what a mentor's betrayal models for a 14-year-old before praising or flagging it.

members.name: Kestrel
members.persona: Rates stories by whether they have the nerve to follow through; a mentor who orchestrated the disaster is the kind of gut-punch that earns his five stars.
